column1: Travel has existed since the beginning of time, when primitive man set out, often traversing great distances in search of game, which provided the food and clothing necessary for his survival.
column2: 旅行自古就有。早期人类为寻找猎物而出行，常常跋涉很远，这些猎物为他们提供了生存所必需的食物和衣物。
column3: since the beginning of time|自古以来

column1: Throughout the course of history, people have travelled for purposes of trade, religious conviction, economic gain, war, migration and other equally compelling motivations.
column2: 纵观历史，贸易、宗教信仰、经济利益、战争、迁徙，以及其他同样强有力的动机，都曾促使人们出行。
column3: Throughout the course of history|纵观历史

column1: In the Roman era, wealthy aristocrats and high government officials also travelled for pleasure.
column2: 在罗马时代，富有的贵族和高级政府官员也会为了娱乐而出行旅行。

column1: Seaside resorts located at Pompeii and Herculaneum afforded citizens the opportunity to escape to their vacation villas in order to avoid the summer heat of Rome.
column2: 庞贝和赫库兰尼姆的海滨度假地，让市民有机会暂时离开罗马，前往自己的度假别墅，以避开罗马夏日的酷热。

column1: Travel, except during the Dark Ages, has continued to grow and, throughout recorded history, has played a vital role in the development of civilisations and their economies.
column2: 旅行活动，除了在黑暗时代之外，一直持续发展，在有记载的历史中始终对文明及其经济的发展起到了至关重要的作用。

column1: Tourism in the mass form as we know it today is a distinctly twentieth-century phenomenon.
column2: 我们今天所熟知的大众旅游现象是一种典型的二十世纪产物。

column1: Historians suggest that the advent of mass tourism began in England during the industrial revolution with the rise of the middle class and the availability of relatively inexpensive transportation.
column2: 历史学家认为，大众旅游最早兴起于工业革命时期的英格兰，当时中产阶级开始崛起，人们也有了相对便宜的交通方式。

column1: The creation of the commercial airline industry following the Second World War and the subsequent development of the jet aircraft in the 1950s signalled the rapid growth and expansion of international travel.
column2: 第二次世界大战后，商业航空业的兴起，以及20世纪50年代喷气式飞机的开发，标志着国际旅行的迅速增长和扩展。

column1: This growth led to the development of a major new industry: tourism.
column2: 这种增长促成了一个新的重要产业的诞生：旅游业。

column1: In turn, international tourism became the concern of a number of world governments since it not only provided new employment opportunities but also produced a means of earning foreign exchange.
column2: 相应地，国际旅游也受到世界上多个国家政府的关注，因为它既提供了新的就业机会，也带来了赚取外汇的途径。

column1: Tourism today has grown significantly in both economic and social importance.
column2: 如今，旅游业在经济和社会方面都取得了显著的发展。

column1: In most industrialised countries over the past few years the fastest growth has been seen in the area of services.
column2: 在过去几年中，大多数工业化国家经济增长最显著的部分是服务业领域的增长。

column1: One of the largest segments of the service industry, although largely unrecognised as an entity in some of these countries, is travel and tourism.
column2: 旅游和旅游业是服务业中规模最大的细分领域之一，不过在部分国家里，这一产业往往未被充分认识到其重要性。

column1: According to the World Travel and Tourism Council (1992), ‘Travel and tourism is the largest industry in the world on virtually any economic measure including value-added capital investment, employment and tax contributions’.
column2: 据世界旅游及旅行理事会（1992年）称，“按几乎任何经济指标来衡量，旅游业都是全球最大的产业，这些指标包括增值资本投资、就业和税收贡献。”
column8: value-added capital investment|增值资本投资

column1: In 1992, the industry’s gross output was estimated to be $3.5 trillion, over 12 per cent of all consumer spending.
column2: 据估算，1992年该行业的总产出为3.5万亿美元，这一数额超过了全部消费支出的12%。
column5: was estimated to be|据估算为

column1: The travel and tourism industry is the world’s largest employer with almost 130 million jobs, or almost 7 per cent of all employees.
column2: 旅游行业是全球最大的就业领域，拥有约1.3亿个工作岗位，占全球员工总数的近7%。

column1: This industry is the world’s leading industrial contributor, producing over 6 per cent of the world’s gross national product and accounting for capital investment in excess of $422 billion in direct, indirect and personal taxes each year.
column2: 这一行业是全球贡献最大的产业，其产值超过全球国民生产总值的6%；在直接税、间接税和个人税方面，该行业每年所涉及的资本投资超过4220亿美元。
column8: gross national product|国民生产总值

column1: Thus, tourism has a profound impact both on the world economy and, because of the educative effect of travel and the effects on employment, on society itself.
column2: 因此，旅游业对世界经济有着深远的影响，同时，由于旅行所具有的教育意义以及其对就业的影响，旅游业也对整个社会产生重要影响。

column1: However, the major problems of the travel and tourism industry that have hidden, or obscured, its economic impact are the diversity and fragmentation of the industry itself.
column2: 然而，旅游行业存在的主要问题在于其自身多样性和碎片化，这些问题掩盖或模糊了其经济影响。

column1: The travel industry includes: hotels, motels and other types of accommodation; restaurants and other food services; transportation services and facilities; amusements, attractions and other leisure facilities; gift shops and a large number of other enterprises.
column2: 旅游业包括旅馆、汽车旅馆及其他类型的住宿设施，餐馆及其他餐饮服务，交通运输服务与设施，各种娱乐活动、游览景点及其他休闲设施，以及礼品店和大量其他企业。

column1: Since many of these businesses also serve local residents, the impact of spending by visitors can easily be overlooked or underestimated.
column2: 由于这些企业中的许多也为当地居民提供服务，因此游客消费所带来的影响很容易被忽视或低估。

column1: In addition, Meis (1992) points out that the tourism industry involves concepts that have remained amorphous to both analysts and decision makers.
column2: 此外，迈斯（1992年）指出，旅游业涉及的一些概念，对分析人士和决策者来说一直都缺乏清晰的界定。

column1: Moreover, in all nations this problem has made it difficult for the industry to develop any type of reliable or credible tourism information base in order to estimate the contribution it makes to regional, national and global economies.
column2: 此外，在各个国家，这个问题都使旅游业难以建立任何可靠或可信的旅游信息库，用以估算旅游业对地区、国家和全球经济的贡献。

column1: However, the nature of this very diversity makes travel and tourism ideal vehicles for economic development in a wide variety of countries, regions or communities.
column2: 然而，恰恰是这种多样性，使旅游活动和旅游业成为众多国家、地区或社区发展经济的理想途径。
column4: this very diversity|恰恰是这种多样性
column5: travel and tourism|旅游活动和旅游业
column8: a wide variety of|多种多样的

column1: Once the exclusive province of the wealthy, travel and tourism have become an institutionalised way of life for most of the population.
column2: 曾经只是富人专属的消遣活动，如今旅游已经成为了大多数人的一种制度化生活方式。

column1: In fact, McIntosh and Goeldner (1990) suggest that tourism has become the largest commodity in international trade for many nations and, for a significant number of other countries, it ranks second or third.
column2: 事实上，麦金托什和戈尔德纳（1990年）认为，在许多国家，旅游已成为国际贸易中最大的一项商品；而在数量相当可观的其他国家，旅游则排在第二或第三位。
column8: a significant number of|相当数量的

column1: For example, tourism is the major source of income in Bermuda, Greece, Italy, Spain, Switzerland and most Caribbean countries.
column2: 例如，旅游业是百慕大、希腊、意大利、西班牙、瑞士以及大多数加勒比国家的主要收入来源。

column1: In addition, Hawkins and Ritchie, quoting from data published by the American Express Company, suggest that the travel and tourism industry is the number one ranked employer in the Bahamas, Brazil, Canada, France, (the former) West Germany, Hong Kong, Italy, Jamaica, Japan, Singapore, the United Kingdom and the United States.
column2: 此外，霍金斯和里奇援引美国运通公司公布的数据指出，在巴哈马、巴西、加拿大、法国、原西德、香港、意大利、牙买加、日本、新加坡、英国和美国，旅游业是雇用人数最多的行业。

column1: However, because of problems of definition, which directly affect statistical measurement, it is not possible with any degree of certainty to provide precise, valid or reliable data about the extent of world-wide tourism participation or its economic impact.
column2: 然而，定义上的问题直接影响统计计量。因此，无论是全球参与旅游的规模，还是旅游的经济影响，都无法有把握地提供精确、有效或可靠的数据。
column3: problems of definition|定义上的问题

column1: In many cases, similar difficulties arise when attempts are made to measure domestic tourism.
column2: 在许多情况下，当试图衡量国内旅游业的发展情况时，也会遇到类似的困难。
